quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should usually keep a minimum following distance of _____.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds behind other vehicles. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Instead, you will notice a change in how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can discourage other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow or stop, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are often slippery.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Use the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Try to move onto the shoulder.
Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Use the center portion of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do on a long ride to prevent fatigue?

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.explanation: Do not take artificial stimulants. You may experience extreme fatigue when they wear off. Instead, dress to protect yourself from bad weather, limit riding to about six hours per day, and take a break at least every two hours.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.explanation: Nearly 40 percent of all riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking. Alcohol is a major cause of fatal motorcycle accidents.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road. This is an important signal when riding in groups.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Move your shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed. Close the throttle and apply both brakes if needed.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should lessen the pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Maintain at least four seconds of following distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is it safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: It is never safe for motorcyclists.
It is usually safe, unless it is raining.
It adds traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oily drippings from cars collect in the center of lanes. This area is usually safe for motorcycles unless the road is wet. The strip is often only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to turn. After you pass the hazard, press the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction.

questions.question: What kind of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right on a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may also leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Stay away from the center of the lane and follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for things that make roads slippery, like oil spots and loose gravel.
